note: Medicine Bow-Routt NF campground at ~8,800 ft beside Freeman Reservoir (non-motorized boats only), 21 mi north of Craig: Hwy 13 north 12 mi, then 8.5 mi of graded gravel on Moffat CR 11 - don't follow GPS routes via CR 40, which campers report gated on private land. Open meadow at the reservoir's southeast end; site 17 has the best lake view. Horse riding, motorbike and hiking trails; California Park nearby (closed to vehicles May 15 - July 1 for sandhill cranes). Formerly run by Moffat County; the FS said it would resume management in June 2026. --Claude
summary: FS page: confirmed FCFS-only (not on recreation.gov), vault toilets, no hookups, $12/$20 exact cash or check, season mid-June - Oct 31. Changed: potable water absent -> false (FS: 'not available'); site count 18 and pull-through cleared (aggregators only - the FS states neither). No agency length figure exists. Pin 150 m from the FS point, on the loops. Note trimmed and rewritten.
flags: RIG-LENGTH: no agency figure. The FS page states no length; aggregators split 25 ft (AllStays, RVingUSA, ParkAdvisor) vs 32 ft (The Dyrt, Good Sam, CampingRoadTrip). The latest own-rig review is a 26-ft Class B+ that 'had no problem at all' (Campendium, 2022-07-18 - older than 3 years), and the same reviewer warns 'The sites are small so if you've got a bigger rig, you need to exercise caution'. Kept; max_rig_ft stays absent.

Road: FS directions give Hwy 13 north 12 mi then 'the graveled road for 8 1/2 miles' (Moffat CR 11); campers describe it as hard-packed and well graded. No 4WD or high-clearance wording. A camper reports GPS routing via CR 40 hits a locked gate on private land.
Missing phone: Hahns Peak/Bears Ears Ranger District 970-870-2299 (FS page itself lists only the forest supervisor's (307) 745-2300).

Management: FS page says 'no longer managed or operated by Moffat County. The Forest Service will resume management in June 2026'; page status 'Site Open'. Fees ($12 vs $20) and the water statement may be stale from the county era.
Potable water: FS says 'not available'; a 2022 review describes a hand-pump well producing potable water west of site 1. Set to false per the agency.
Waterfront (stored lakeview) stands: the loops sit in open meadow ~100-200 m from the reservoir's southeast shore with no screen; the dam is at the far (west) end, so the campground is not below it.
